elements.quote: Worldwide, surgery related deaths within 30 days of the procedure accounts the third contributor among all causes of deaths, with an estimated 4.2 million people annually and half of these deaths occur in low and middle income countries.
elements.reason: The Introduction provides some context on the burden of surgical deaths, but the retrieved evidence does not show a description of the current state of knowledge on SSI after cesarean section in Ethiopia or explicit uncertainties/gaps in existing knowledge.
No retrieved evidence from the Introduction explains the importance of or need for conducting this review; only a general statistic on surgery-related deaths is provided (text_3).

The retrieved evidence contains no statement identifying or citing previous similar systematic reviews or explaining how the current review updates or differs from them. The PROSPERO check (text_10) addresses duplication of ongoing registrations, not the need for the review relative to existing published reviews, so the conditional requirement cannot be considered satisfied or demonstrably not applicable.

This is a review of prevalence and predictors (prognostic/etiological associations) of SSI after cesarean section, not a review of intervention effects, so no mechanism of action needs to be described.
The review addresses prevalence and predictors of an outcome, not a complex intervention or delivery context, so a logic model of intervention components is not applicable.
